title: One function, many kinds of type
description:
Write one template, `std::string inspect(const T& value)`, that behaves differently depending on what `T` is. Use `if constexpr` with type traits: only the matching branch is compiled for each type.

| `T` is | Result |
|---|---|
| `bool` | `"bool true"` or `"bool false"` |
| any other integral type | `"integer 42"` |
| a floating-point type | `"decimal 2.500000"` |
| a pointer | `"null pointer"`, or `"pointer to "` followed by `inspect` of what it points at |
| has `.size()` | `"container of 3"` |
| anything else | `"unknown"` |

Check `bool` before the other integers (`bool` is an integral type), and pointers before containers.
hints: Write an `if constexpr` chain in the order of the table: `std::is_same_v<T, bool>` first, then `std::is_integral_v<T>`, `std::is_floating_point_v<T>`, `std::is_pointer_v<T>`.
For "has `.size()`", use a `requires` expression as the condition: `else if constexpr (requires { value.size(); })`. Each branch is compiled only for the types that reach it.
